title: Losing the signal
topic: Raising concerns about systems and safety
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the labour ward. The midwives tell you that one of the CTG monitors keeps losing the fetal heart signal. They reported it a week ago but were told to "manage".

A woman in established labour, with risk factors that need continuous monitoring, is on that monitor now.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Tell the midwives to manage as they were told.
options.detailed: A monitor that loses the signal can't be relied on for women who need continuous monitoring.

options.text: Try to repair the monitor yourself.
options.brief: Not your role, and it may not work.
options.detailed: Equipment repairs should be done by the right technical staff.

options.text: Tell the woman the monitor is unreliable.
options.brief: May alarm her without solving the problem.
options.detailed: She should know if her monitoring changes, but the priority is to fix it.

options.text: Wait to see whether the signal drops again before acting.
options.detailed: The problem is known and recurring.

options.text: Ask the midwife to move the woman to a working monitor.
options.brief: She needs reliable continuous monitoring now.
options.detailed: Continuous monitoring is recommended for her. A faulty monitor puts her baby at risk.

options.text: Post about the faulty monitor in the junior doctors' group chat.
options.brief: Not an effective or appropriate way to raise a concern.
options.detailed: This doesn't reach the people who can fix it.

options.text: Report the faulty monitor as an incident.
options.brief: Creates a formal record of the problem.
options.detailed: Informal reports have been ignored. A formal report creates a record and triggers a review.

options.text: Raise the problem with the labour ward consultant.
options.brief: A senior can make sure it's fixed or replaced.
options.detailed: The consultant can escalate it and make sure the faulty monitor is withdrawn until repaired.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you act on an equipment problem that is putting a patient at risk, and make sure it is formally addressed.
explanation.keyDetails: The monitor keeps losing the signal. It has been reported informally. A woman who needs continuous monitoring is on it.
explanation.reasoning: [E] protects the woman and her baby now, [G] creates a formal record, and [H] gets senior action. The distractors accept the risk ([A], [D]), act outside your role ([B]), alarm her ([C]), or use the wrong route ([F]).
explanation.competing: [C] seems honest, and she should know about changes, but moving her to a working monitor matters more.
